correctness.rationale: Exact ordered arclength convolution yields the complete density and its hinge expansion. The small-distance value and slope identify scale and degree; distributional second differentiation gives the precise signed atomic measure. The smallest differing arm length contradiction proves global uniqueness for every positive real multiset because pair-sum atoms at that length depend only on shorter known arms. The residual peeling algorithm explicitly recovers canceled knots. Rational exact tests cover nontrivial collisions; seeded random arclength pairs corroborate but are not used as universal proof.

originality.rationale: The exact uniform-arclength pair-distance law and all-parameter global rigidity of finite metric stars are not a consequence of the accessible earlier results. The 2018 metric-graph result advertises local injectivity, not a complete global star classification, and the 2024 measured-tree construction concerns realizability with different sampling measures. Algebraic reconstruction at fully canceled arm-length curvature knots supplies the key non-generic distinction. Full-text access limitations create residual historical-priority uncertainty.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves a natural scalar-distance-histogram inverse problem for all finite positively weighted stars with no genericity assumptions. It identifies a hidden cancellation mechanism (arms 1,2,3) and constructs exact recovery despite loss of a visible singularity, strengthening naive curvature-knot tomography. Such all-parameter structural rigidity informs when a pair-distance law suffices for geometric identification, without claiming universality among general trees or statistical robustness.
